title: Surjective homomorphisms of equal-dimensional abelian varieties are isogenies
statement: Let $k$ be any field [def-weil-field], let $A,B$ be abelian varieties over $k$ [def-sc-abelian-variety] with $\dim A=\dim B$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], and let $f:A\to B$ be a homomorphism of $k$-group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme]. Then $f$ is an isogeny [def-sc-isogeny] if and only if it is surjective on underlying scheme points. In particular an endomorphism of $A$ that is not an isogeny is not dominant.

source.place: Chapter I, Proposition 7.1 (a) iff (b), printed p.32, and its proper-image argument

proof.text: If $f$ is an isogeny, it is surjective by the definition [def-sc-isogeny]. This implication needs no dimension assumption.

source.place: Chapter I, Proposition 7.1, printed p.32: (a) iff (b) and the closed-image argument

proof.text: Conversely assume $f$ is surjective. Let $I\hookrightarrow B$ be its scheme-theoretic image and $K=\ker f$. The hypotheses of [lem-sc-image-subgroup] hold: $A$ is proper and $B$ is separated and of finite type, by [def-sc-abelian-variety]. That node gives the factorization through $I$ with $A\to I$ surjective. Since $f$ is surjective too, the closed immersion $I\hookrightarrow B$ is surjective on points. By [def-weil-closed-immersion] it is therefore a homeomorphism, so $\dim I=\dim B$. Now [lem-sfb-abelian-hom-image-dimension] gives $\dim A=\dim I+\dim K$. The dimensions of $A$ and $I$ are finite by [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type], because both are abelian varieties and hence of finite type. Also $K$ is nonempty: the identity of $A$ maps to the identity of $B$, giving a $k$-point of $K$ by [def-sc-group-scheme]. Substituting $\dim I=\dim B=\dim A$ in the dimension formula and cancelling this finite dimension gives $\dim K=0$.

source.place: Chapter I, Proposition 7.1, printed p.32: (a) iff (b) and the closed-image argument

proof.text: By [lem-sc-kernel-subgroup], $K\hookrightarrow A$ is a closed subgroup scheme. Apply [lem-pc-zero-dimensional-closed-subscheme-finite] to this closed subscheme of the finite-type $k$-scheme $A$, using $\dim K=0$ from step 2. It follows that $K$ is finite over $k$. Thus $f$ is a surjective homomorphism with finite scheme-theoretic kernel, which is exactly an isogeny by [def-sc-isogeny]. No reducedness of $K$ or separability of $f$ has been assumed.

source.place: Tag 06LH, lemma-algebraic-scheme-dim-0; applied to the kernel in Milne AV I Proposition 7.1

proof.text: For an endomorphism $f:A\to A$, [lem-weil-pbc-proper-to-separated] applies over $\operatorname{Spec}k$: its source is proper and its target is separated by [def-sc-abelian-variety]. Hence $f$ is proper, and [lem-weil-pbc-proper-closed-image] says that $f(A)$ is closed. If $f$ were dominant, its image would also be dense, so it would equal $A$. The equivalence proved in steps 1–3, with $B=A$, would make $f$ an isogeny. Taking the contrapositive proves the final assertion.
